posts.title: Cycling Through Al-Andalus: Documenting Andalusia’s Islamic Heritage
posts.description: Paul Ammann cycles through Andalusia to document its Islamic heritage. The route connects rural mosques, frontier castles, and medieval bathhouses, tracing the architectural remains of al-Andalus. The post Cycling Through Al-Andalus: Documenting Andalusia’s Islamic Heritage first appeared on Arabic for Nerds and is written by Paul Ammann .

posts.title: Religion, debt, and the city: one Arabic root (د-ي-ن), or three different stories?
posts.description: At first glance, دِين (religion), دَيْن (debt) and مَدِينَة (city) look neatly related. Classical dictionaries, Aramaic and Persian make the story much less simple. The post Religion, debt, and the city: one Arabic root (د-ي-ن), or three different stories? first appeared on Arabic for Nerds and is written by Marnix Demesmaeker .

posts.title: A Hell of a Sentence: The word إِحْدَى ("one") in Sura 74:35
posts.description: How much trouble can "one" cause? In Quran 74:35, it comes with a displaced letter, a feminine pronoun, and a trail that leads past the moon, night and dawn to Hellfire. Three words, centuries of debate, and plenty to put under the grammatical microscope. The post A Hell of a Sentence: The word إِحْدَى ("one") in Sura 74:35 first appeared on Arabic for Nerds and is written by Gerald Drißner .
